title: Blueprints-as-Code: tenant batch/cache defaults + lightweight quant fallthrough
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for tenant-level safe defaults for batching/caching and a simple CPU fallback path using low-precision quant profiles to avoid outages when GPU capacity is constrained. Summary: add a "Blueprints-as-Code" format (YAML) for tenant defaults, wire a small in-runtime defaults loader, and introduce two compact quant fallthrough profiles (int8-fast, int8-conservative) plus a migration that applies a conservative safe default to existing tenants. Includes a CLI import/export for blueprints and a docs page. Checklist: [x] define YAML schema and examples; [x] implement loader and validation; [x] implement quant fallthrough selection logic; [x] add integration tests; [x] add CLI import/export; [x] add docs and examples. Risk: non-breaking by default (only applied to tenants opted-in by the migration), conservative fallback selected automatically when GPU pool is unavailable. Related: ENG-5042 (tenant defaults work), SUP-3301 (customer incident for GPU shortage).

conversation: Luca Romano (reviewer): Can we make the YAML schema forward compatible? Suggest adding a 'version' top-level key and a clear migration path.
Maya Chen (author): Added 'schema_version: 1' to examples and loader checks; loader will ignore unknown top-level keys unless 'strict: true' is set.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Please add telemetry for 'blueprint_applied' and 'quant_fallback_used' to the per-tenant metrics so we can measure impact.
Maya Chen (author): Telemetry hooks added in quant_fallback.go and blueprint_loader.go; added unit tests asserting metric emission.
Samir Patel (reviewer): Concern about silent fallbacks impacting latency-sensitive routes. Recommend opt-in for latency SLO routes.
Maya Chen (author): Added 'route_overrides' in the YAML and a guard that prevents automatic quant fallback for routes marked 'slo:latency' unless tenant explicitly allows 'allow_fallback_slo: true'.
